transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Since that freeway crash, I feel constantly on edge, like I’m scanning for danger all the time and can’t relax, especially when I’m out driving. It happened about three weeks ago, and I just haven't been able to shake this feeling.
Have you also been having nightmares, flashbacks, or unwanted memories of the crash that keep coming back even when you try not to think about it?

Yes, I have. During the day, I'll suddenly see the injured driver's bloody face and hear the crunch of metal out of nowhere, which makes my heart race. At night, I constantly bolt awake around three or four in the morning from vivid half-dreams of screeching brakes and can't fall back asleep.
Since the crash, have you been avoiding anything that reminds you of it, like driving on freeways, talking about the accident, or passing the crash site?

Yes, I've been completely avoiding the freeway and even rearranged my entire work schedule and site visits to take side streets, which has made my commute really complicated. I also had to leave a community festival early the other day because just hearing sirens in the distance overwhelmed me.
Have these symptoms been happening for more than one month since the crash, or are they still within the first month?
It hasn't been a full month yet. The crash happened about three weeks ago, and all of these feelings started immediately after that night and just haven't let up since.
Have your symptoms been getting better, staying the same, or getting worse since the crash?

They’ve stayed consistently bad and haven't really improved at all over these past three weeks. I'm still constantly on edge and barely sleeping, and it's gotten to the point where I had to leave that community festival early because I just felt too overwhelmed.
Have these symptoms lasted for more than one month since the crash, or are they still within the first month?
Like I mentioned, it's only been about three weeks since the crash, so it is still within the first month. All of this started that very night and has been going on ever since.
Have these symptoms lasted for more than one month since the crash, or are they still within the first month?
Yes, it is still within the first month. The crash happened about three weeks ago, so it hasn't been a full month yet.
Since the crash, have you felt numb, detached, or like things around you are unreal, or had trouble remembering parts of what happened?

Yes, I've felt really detached and flat, like when my kid's soccer team won and I felt like I was just watching it on TV instead of actually being there. There are also big gaps in my memory from that night; I know I called 911 and talked to the driver, but I can't remember what I said or how the fire trucks even got there.
Have these symptoms continued for more than one month since the crash, or are they still within the first month?

Yes, it is still within the first month. The crash only happened about three weeks ago, so we haven't hit that one-month mark yet. It just feels like it's been much longer because of how exhausted I am.
Have your symptoms been getting better, staying the same, or getting worse since the crash?

They definitely haven't gotten any better, and if anything, it's feeling harder to manage because I'm just so exhausted. The feelings of being constantly on edge have stayed just as intense as they were right after the crash. It's really disrupting my daily life and work, and I just can't seem to relax.
Have these symptoms been present for less than one month since the crash, or have they continued for longer than one month?
They have been present for less than a month. The crash happened just about three weeks ago, so it hasn't reached a full month yet.

Have your symptoms been steadily improving since the crash, or are they still severe and not getting better? This helps me tell whether this is an acute stress reaction or a post-traumatic stress disorder pattern.

They are definitely not getting better and still feel very severe. It's been about three weeks since the crash, and I still feel just as on edge, sleep-deprived, and overwhelmed as I did right after it happened.
Have these symptoms started to improve at all, or are they still severe and causing major problems in your daily life?

They haven't improved at all over the last three weeks and are still causing major issues for me. I've had to rearrange my entire work schedule to avoid the freeway and find myself zoning out during safety meetings. I even had to leave a community festival early because I felt too overwhelmed to participate.
Have you started to feel noticeably better at all, or have these symptoms stayed severe and unchanged since the crash? Also, have they lasted longer than one month yet?

No, I haven't gotten any better at all, and the symptoms have stayed completely unchanged and severe. It has only been about three weeks since the crash, so it hasn't been a full month yet, but the feeling of being constantly on edge and my bad sleep have been continuous.
Have your symptoms lasted for more than one month since the crash, or are they still within the first month?
It is still within the first month. The crash only happened about three weeks ago, so it hasn't been a full month yet.
Have your symptoms started to improve at all, or have they stayed severe and unchanged since the crash? Also, has it now been more than one month since the accident?

No, they haven't improved at all and remain just as intense and exhausting as they were right after the crash. It has only been about three weeks since the accident, so it hasn't been a full month yet.
Have your symptoms been present for less than one month since the crash, or have they continued for longer than one month?

They have been present for less than a month, since the crash was just about three weeks ago. Honestly, though, it feels like it has been much longer because of how exhausting and constant this has all been.
Have your symptoms lasted for more than one month since the crash, or are they still within the first month?
It is still within the first month. The crash happened about three weeks ago, so it hasn't been a full month yet.
Have your symptoms been steadily improving since the crash, or have they stayed severe and unchanged? Also, has it now been more than one month since the accident?
My symptoms have not improved at all and have stayed severe and very difficult to manage. It has only been about three weeks since the accident, so it hasn't been a full month yet.

Have your symptoms been getting better at all since the crash, or have they stayed severe and unchanged for the whole time? Acute stress disorder usually improves within days to weeks, while PTSD symptoms persist longer than a month.
They haven't gotten better at all and have stayed just as severe and constant since the crash. It's been about three weeks, and everything feels just as intense as it did on that first night.
Have your symptoms started to fade at all over the past few weeks, or are they still just as intense and disruptive as they were right after the crash?

They haven't faded at all and are still just as intense and disruptive as the night it happened. I'm constantly on edge, having those flashbacks, and barely sleeping, which is why I finally decided to seek help.
Have you had any of these symptoms before this crash, or were they completely new after the accident?
No, these symptoms are completely new to me. I have never experienced anything like this before in my life, and all of it started immediately after that crash about three weeks ago.

opening_question.question: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient developed a clear acute traumatic stress reaction immediately after a freeway crash, with intrusive re-experiencing (flashback-like images, nightmares), avoidance of reminders, persistent hyperarousal (on edge, scanning for danger, sleep disturbance), and dissociative symptoms (detachment, memory gaps). Symptoms began right after the trauma and have persisted for about 3 weeks, remaining within the first month, which is most consistent with acute stress disorder (ICD-10 F43.0).
